title: RealHerdr::agent_wait reads herdr's actual reply shape, and every new real parse is pinned to a captured reply
action: SHIP-BLOCKING. `RealHerdr::agent_wait` (run.rs:590) reads the WRONG JSON path, so it returns `None` for every real herdr reply, the ready gate never sees `idle` or `done`, and EVERY `bee herding run` now dies after 60s with `agent never reported ready within 60s (ready-wait)`. Reproduced live three times against a healthy agy pane sitting at its prompt, solo and in parallel. The whole herding path is broken on this branch right now. The code does `v.get("result").and_then(|r| r.get("agent_status").or_else(|| r.get("status")))`. Here is the ACTUAL reply, captured live from `herdr agent wait accept-solo-1 --until idle --until done --timeout 200`, trimmed: `{"id":"cli:agent:wait","result":{"agent":{"agent":"agy","agent_status":"done","interactive_ready":true,"name":"accept-solo-1","pane_id":"w4:p2J",...},"type":"agent_info"}}`. The status lives at `result.agent.agent_status`, one level deeper than the code looks. Fix the parse. Keep the fail-safe contract exactly as the doc comment states — `None` on herdr missing, an unparseable body, or no settle inside the window — and keep the same shape as `RealHerdr::agent_status` (run.rs:570-578), which parses `result.agents[]` correctly and is the model to follow. WHY THIS SURVIVED THE SUITE, and what to do about it: `FakeHerdr::agent_wait` returns a value the test configured, so every test exercised the SEAM and none exercised the PARSE. Add parse-level unit tests that feed the real captured JSON text through the same extraction the impl uses — for `agent_wait` the reply above, and for `agent_prompt`'s success envelope this captured reply from `herdr agent prompt <job> <text> --wait --until working --timeout 5000`: `{"id":"cli:agent:prompt","result":{"agent":{"agent":"agy","agent_status":"working","name":"accept-solo-1",...},"type":"agent_info"}}`. Structure it so the extraction is a small pure function the impl calls and the test can call with a `&str` of JSON — do not spawn any process in a test. Do the same for any OTHER parse this feature added against a live herdr reply; `agent_status`, `pane_rect`, `pane_alive` and `pane_read` predate it and already work, so leave them alone. Also re-read `is_agent_prompt_stalled` (run.rs:733 area) and make sure it matches the string herdr actually returns on a stalled submission, not a guessed one — if it cannot be verified from herdr's own documented wording, say so in a comment rather than asserting it silently.

truths: agent_wait extracts the status from result.agent.agent_status and returns it
A parse-level test feeds the captured live agent wait reply through the real extraction, not through FakeHerdr
A parse-level test covers the captured agent prompt success envelope the same way
